personas.name: Dana, backend developer
personas.background: Builds the support tool at a small online shop. Uses the OpenAI and Claude APIs at work, so to Dana a "model" means a large language model you send a prompt to, and "classify" means asking a chat model a question.
personas.goal: Find out whether this can tag incoming support tickets as billing, shipping or technical, and how to call it from a Node.js backend.
personas.knows: HTTP APIs, JSON, Node.js, Docker. Has never run a model locally and does not know what GLiNER is.

personas.name: Ravi, front-end developer
personas.background: Builds React apps. Wants features that work in the browser with no server.
personas.goal: Find out whether text can be classified entirely in the browser inside a React app, and what it costs the user in download size and speed.
personas.knows: React, Vite, fetch, CORS, Web Workers in theory. Little machine learning.

personas.name: Priya, product manager
personas.background: Evaluating tools for a customer feedback team. Not a programmer, but reads documentation and can paste a command if told exactly what to type.
personas.goal: Decide whether this is accurate enough for sorting customer feedback and whether customer text stays private, then explain that to her manager.
personas.knows: Spreadsheets, survey tools, the idea of AI chat assistants. No command line experience beyond copying commands.

personas.name: Marek, ML engineer
personas.background: Has trained text classifiers and used Hugging Face zero-shot pipelines. Skeptical of accuracy claims without methodology.
personas.goal: Find what model this is, how it was evaluated, how confidence scores are calibrated, and whether the numbers on the site are reproducible.
personas.knows: Transformers, NLI zero-shot classification, ONNX, evaluation metrics, calibration.
